issue.summary: Friendly Names for Attributes Not Displayed Consistently in Web Editor
issue.description:
Source-preserved issue and human-review scope:
- Full Tags View shows the original attribute name instead of the configured friendly name.
- The Condition Attributes panel does not show the configured friendly name.
- The Right Panel loses the friendly name after the attribute is applied.
- For a custom attribute added to the DTD, display its configured friendly name. If no friendly name is configured, display the raw attribute name. Validate this in Full Tags View, the Condition Attributes panel, and the Right Panel.
- When an attribute's friendly name is added, updated, or removed in Workspace Settings, the change should automatically appear in Full Tags View, the Condition Attributes panel, and the Right Panel without a page reload.
- This functionality should work for any valid conditional attribute added to /libs/fmdita/config/condAttrList.csv. Display its friendly name when configured; otherwise, display the raw attribute name.
- Verify friendly names are applied for the logged-in user, as this is a user-level setting.
- Verify that when Use only above attributes is enabled, only configured attributes are displayed for all elements.
- Verify configured friendly names are preserved and continue to work after an AEM Guides build upgrade.
- Verify the existing friendly-name functionality for elements is not affected.
- For condition presets, should friendly attribute names be displayed when configured?
- In a DITAVAL file's attribute dropdown, should attributes use their raw names or configured friendly names?
- In Preview mode, should attributes use their raw names or configured friendly names?

feature_classification.rationale: The ticket changes how a configuration-backed attribute list is discovered and how its labels render across multiple UI consumers and scopes.

PERFORMANCE.reason: The inspected change resolves one display label per rendered attribute, and the Jira provides no scale, latency, throughput, or bulk-workload requirement.

SECURITY.reason: The inspected behavior changes displayed labels and does not add credential, secret, trust-boundary, or data-exposure behavior.

CONCURRENCY.reason: The Jira requires one open editor to reflect a saved setting without reload but supplies no simultaneous-writer or concurrent-update contract.

update_paths: Open Tag View receives an attribute friendly-name update when the cross-package command exists.

versioned_models: Pre-upgrade and post-upgrade Editor profile configuration
constraints: Only DTD-valid attributes are offered for the selected element.
Already-applied attributes remain visible when choices are restricted.

The cached PR ref adds friendly lookup and fallback in the attribute, condition, and applied-row models.
Current configuration code saves attribute mappings under an active folder profile with global fallback.
Human review requests that friendly names apply to the logged-in user as a user-level setting.
Starling checks the apps overlay before libs and legacy XML before CSV.
